verdict.summary: The auth flow has two meaningful performance issues: telemetry KV writes are awaited in the request path (adding ~20-50ms per auth response), and GitHub fetch calls have no timeout (Workers hang during GitHub degradation). Both are fixable with ctx.waitUntil and AbortController respectively.
verdict.confidenceReason: The I/O topology is clear from the diff; the missing-timeout and blocking-telemetry patterns are unambiguous, though actual latency impact depends on KV/GitHub response times in production.

findings.headline: Telemetry KV writes block every auth response
findings.body: Every `await writeAuthEvent(...)` in `handleGitHubAuthKickoff` (line ~100) and `handleGitHubAuthCallback` (lines ~131, ~148, ~170, ~191, ~210, ~241, ~262) adds a KV PUT round-trip to the response latency. Telemetry is non-essential and already wrapped in try/catch — it should be fire-and-forget via `ctx.waitUntil`. The handlers don't currently receive `ExecutionContext`, so `ctx` must be threaded from `src/index.ts` where it's available. On the kickoff path this is a ~50% latency reduction (2 KV writes → 1); on the callback path it saves ~20ms per error path. Fix: add `ctx?: ExecutionContext` to both handler signatures, pass `ctx` from the router, and replace `await writeAuthEvent(...)` with `ctx?.waitUntil(writeAuthEvent(...))`.

findings.headline: No timeout on GitHub fetch calls — Workers hang during upstream degradation
findings.body: The two `fetch()` calls to GitHub (token exchange at line ~163, user profile at line ~215) have no `AbortController` timeout. If GitHub is slow or unresponsive, the Worker blocks on I/O wait until Cloudflare's connection-level timeout (which can be tens of seconds). During a GitHub partial outage, many concurrent auth callbacks could pile up, consuming Worker subrequest concurrency. Fix: add `const ac = new AbortController(); const timer = setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 10_000);` and pass `signal: ac.signal` to both fetch calls, clearing the timer after each resolves.

findings.headline: Sequential KV DELETE blocks token exchange in callback
findings.body: In `handleGitHubAuthCallback`, the state nonce `await env.OPENCLAW_STATE.delete(...)` (line ~140) is awaited before the token exchange `fetch()` (line ~163). These are independent — the DELETE is a best-effort cleanup, and the token exchange doesn't depend on its completion. Running them concurrently saves ~20ms. Fix: start the DELETE as a fire-and-forget via `ctx.waitUntil(env.OPENCLAW_STATE.delete(...))` or run it in `Promise.all` with the fetch.

findings.headline: Missing test for `/auth/me` endpoint (returns 401/200, omits `githubInstallations`)
findings.body: The spec (v2 LOCKED) test #22 requires: `/auth/me` returns 401 without session, returns 200 with session, omits `githubInstallations` in v1. No test exists in the diff. This is a public API endpoint that exposes user identity; an untested regression could leak data or break the marketing site's bootstrap fetch. Add integration tests in `tests/auth-routing.test.ts` (or a new file) that mock `requireSession` and verify the JSON shape.

findings.headline: Missing test for `/auth/welcome` endpoint (happy path + invalid/expired session)
findings.body: The spec tests #7–9 require: welcome happy path (valid cookie → renders HTML with login), welcome rejects invalid cookie (302 to /), welcome rejects expired session (302 to /). No test exists. The route uses `requireSession` and `renderWelcomePage`; untested changes could break the post-login landing page. Add tests that mock `requireSession` to return a session or null and verify the response status and body.

findings.headline: Missing test for concurrent same-state callbacks (KV eventual consistency edge case)
findings.body: Spec test #21 explicitly requires: simulate two callback Promises both reading the same nonce; one wins (KV mocked to return value once then null) — second fails `state_invalid`. This is a non-trivial branch that the spec calls out as a risk. The current tests only cover the single-callback path. Add a test that calls `handleGitHubAuthCallback` twice with the same state, using a KV mock that returns the state on the first call and null on the second, and asserts the second returns 400 `state_invalid`.

findings.headline: Missing test for 501 stub routes (`/auth/google`, `/auth/email`, etc.)
findings.body: Spec test #15 requires: `/auth/google`, `/auth/email`, `/auth/gitlab`, `/auth/bitbucket`, `/auth/azure` all return 501 with a plain-text body. No test exists. While simple, these routes are part of the public surface and should be tested to ensure they don't accidentally 404 or return unexpected content. Add a parameterized test in `tests/auth-routing.test.ts`.

findings.headline: Missing test for telemetry event shape verification
findings.body: Spec test #16 requires: `kickoff`, `callback_success`, `callback_failed`, `logout` events written; verify shape. The `writeAuthEvent` function is called but never tested. The tests mock KV and check `kv.put` for state nonce, but not for auth events. Add tests that verify the correct event object is written to KV with the expected fields and TTL.

log.query:
feat(phase5): GitHub user OAuth + session for app.sigilix.ai

Closes [ARC-163](https://linear.app/arc-and-anchor/issue/ARC-163).

The marketing CTAs on `app.sigilix.ai` send users to `/auth/github` etc.; the Worker had no handlers, every click 404'd. This wires GitHub user-to-server OAuth + an opaque server-side session.

## Routes
| Method | Path | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/auth/github` | kickoff (state nonce + state cookie + 302) |
| GET | `/auth/github/callback` | validate + exchange code + create session |
| GET | `/auth/welcome` | render minimal authenticated HTML |
| GET | `/auth/me` | JSON {login, githubUserId} |
| POST | `/auth/logout` | delete session + clear cookie |
| GET | `/auth/{google,email,gitlab,bitbucket,azure}` | 501 stubs |

## Security model (per [v2 LOCKED spec](.claude/handoff/arc-phase5-auth-spec-v2-LOCKED.md))
- **AES-GCM** access-token encryption at rest with **AAD = `auth_session:<id>`** — a misplaced ciphertext can never decrypt as another session's token (Codex catch on v1)
- **Browser-bound state**: KV nonce AND a `__Host-sigilix_oauth_state` cookie must both match in the callback. Defends against the login-CSRF where an attacker pairs their own code with a stolen state in the victim's browser (Codex catch on v1)
- **`safeRedirectAfter()`** rejects scheme-relative URLs (`//evil.com`), backslashes, NUL bytes, encoded slashes that look in-app but break out, and absolute URLs. URL-parse + same-origin check as defense in depth (Codex catch on v1)
- **`__Host-`** cookie prefix on both auth cookies — strictest browser semantics, no `Domain` attribute, sibling subdomains can't read
- **HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax** — JS can't read the cookie; CSRF on cross-site POST blocked; top-level GET (GitHub callback) still works
- **30-day sliding session TTL**, refreshed on each authenticated request
- **Strict CSP** on `/auth/welcome` (`default-src self; script-src none`)

## Files
- `src/lib/auth-session.ts` — AES-GCM, base64url, cookie + KV helpers
- `src/lib/auth-oauth-github.ts` — kickoff + callback + redirect validator
- `src/lib/auth-middleware.ts` — `requireSession()`
- `src/lib/auth-welcome.ts` — `/auth/welcome` HTML render

## Env vars (new, all optional — `/auth/*` returns 503 if missing)
- `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`
- `GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
- `OPENCLAW_SESSION_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (32 bytes, base64url)
- `OPENCLAW_BASE_URL` (default `https://app.sigilix.ai`)

## Tests: 489 → 532 (+43)
Covers AAD round-trip, AAD mismatch rejection, IV freshness, key size validation, browser-binding state-mismatch, KV state-invalid, code_exchange + user_fetch failure paths, redirectAfter open-redirect blockers (`//evil.com`, `/\\evil.com`, `javascript:`, encoded variants, NUL injections, absolute URLs), in-app paths preserved with query + fragment.

## Sign-off
- Codex r1: 'do not ship' with 5 blockers — all integrated into v2 (AAD, browser-bound state, KV consistency caveat documented, strict redirectAfter, tests)
- Kimi K2.6 r1: 'ship with 4 tweaks' — all integrated (`/auth/welcome`, `OPENCLAW_BASE_URL`, underscored KV prefixes, `user:email` scope)

## Test plan
- [ ] After merge + deploy, set the 4 secrets via `wrangler secret put`
- [ ] Add `https://app.sigilix.ai/auth/github/callback` to the GitHub App's User authorization callback URL list
- [ ] Manually walk through `/auth/github` → consent → `/auth/welcome` shows the user's GitHub login
- [ ] Try the open-redirect attack vectors and confirm they fall back to `/auth/welcome`
- [ ] Run `POST /auth/logout` and confirm session is cleared
